subject: BrightDesk trial — structured output + retry spec and next steps
messages:
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightdesk.com>, Diego Ramos <diego.r@brightdesk.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: BrightDesk trial — structured output + retry spec and next steps

Elena / Diego — thanks again for the call this morning. Quick recap and recommended next steps so the team has a single place to reference: 

Summary of fit (short):
- Workload: structured invoice extraction + automated actions (create invoice, assign to owner).
- Quality bar: field-level exactness >= 95% on invoice_number / totals; schema compliance required for downstream automation.
- Latency target: 250ms median for single-turn function call; acceptable up to 600ms for complex invoices.

Model recommendations (initial):
- Redwood-2-13B-q8 (high-precision, deterministic decoding for schema output) — start here for best schema compliance.
- Llama-3-8B-4bit (cost-efficient baseline) — use as fallback / cost gate for lower-throughput routes.

Benchmark and artifacts I attached: prompt set (brightdesk_prompt_set_v1.jsonl), benchmark summary (bd_benchmark_summary_q2.csv), and the JSON schema we suggest for the invoice tool (invoice_jsonschema_v2.json). Also linking an internal eval dashboard for the trial.

Tool / function-calling guidance (short):
- Single function: create_invoice(invoice: JSON) -> {status, id, errors[]}. We recommend the model return only the JSON object; Redwood runtime will validate against invoice_jsonschema_v2.json.
- Schema enforcement: enable strict schema validation on the endpoint and return a 4xx style validation error if schema mismatches.
- Retries: client-side retry policy for transient execution errors (5xx, timeouts). Recommended: 3 attempts, exponential backoff (200ms -> 400ms -> 800ms) + randomized jitter. For idempotent operations (read-only or create-if-not-exists with unique client_token) it's safe to retry; for non-idempotent operations prefer server-side dedupe token.

Proposed next steps / timeline:
1) You drop the sample invoice corpus (we already have a small set from the call).
2) We run a 3-day baseline using Redwood-2-13B-q8 and the provided prompt set; we'll deliver per-field precision/recall, latency distribution, and malformed-schema rate. (ETA: 3 business days after we receive corpus)
3) Tech sync to review results and decide canary plan (T+4).

Meeting cadence: propose Wednesday 5/24 10am PT for result review — I’ll send a calendar hold once you confirm.

If helpful I included a short acceptance checklist in the Drive link: field accuracy targets, max malformed outputs, and rollout gating criteria.

Thanks — short action items for BrightDesk: share corpus + confirm Wed 5/24 if that works.

—
Karthik Iyer

Thanks Karthik — this is great and aligns well with our goals. A couple of clarifying questions before we drop the full corpus: 

1) Schema validation: if the model returns a syntactically valid JSON that still fails business-level checks (e.g., total != sum of line items), do you recommend rejecting at the model layer or letting a downstream service handle business validation?

2) Retries: for the endpoint you suggest, if the create_invoice call is non-idempotent, can Redwood pass back a dedupe token (we can provide client_token) so retries are safe?

3) Prompt tuning: the team asked whether you expect any small prompt-format changes (system messages / few-shot examples) to drastically change schema compliance.

We can confirm Wed 5/24 10am PT. I’ll upload a 100-invoice sample and a separate set with more edge cases by EOD Monday.

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>

Cc: Elena Soto <elena.soto@brightdesk.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 17 May 2028 17:05:10 -0700
Subject: Re: BrightDesk trial — structured output + retry spec and next steps

Looping in the technical details so BrightDesk has it in thread. A few notes from infra/evals: 

- Business-level validation: recommend a two-stage approach. Stage 1: strict JSON Schema validation in runtime to catch structural issues (missing fields, wrong types). Stage 2: downstream business validators (microservice) that check arithmetic / cross-field invariants (totals, tax logic). We’ll flag "business_validation_fail" in the response error array so you can decide accept/reject flows.

- Dedupe token: Redwood endpoints support an optional client_token header. If provided we will attach it to the request and the platform will ensure at-most-once semantics for the duration of the request TTL (48h). For create-type operations include a client_token from the caller.

- Prompt stability: small changes in the system prompt (clarity, explicit "output must be valid JSON") significantly increase schema compliance. Few-shot examples that show malformed->fixed pairs also help. We included both in brightdesk_prompt_set_v1.jsonl.

- Benchmarks: attached bd_benchmark_summary_q2.csv — short summary: Redwood-2-13B-q8 achieved 96.7% per-field exactness on the sample corpus with a malformed-schema rate of 1.2%. Llama-3-8B-4bit was ~90.3% exactness and 3.8% malformed. We’ll ship detailed per-field CSVs after the trial run.

Technical config recommendation (initial):
- endpoint: /v1/functions/create_invoice?model=redwood-2-13b-q8&strict_schema=true
- runtime validation: true (reject malformed JSON)
- retry semantics (client): max_attempts=3, backoff_base=200ms, backoff_factor=2, jitter=full
- acceptance gate: malformed_rate < 2% AND per-field exactness >= 95%

I’ll start the baseline job as soon as we have the corpus — should be back within 3 business days.

—
Monica Patel
Senior Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Elena — quick note on procurement and acceptance criteria so your finance/procurement folks have clarity: 

Procurement asks / notes:
- Trial terms: 14-day eval, no charge, up to 100k tokens. If you want extended reserved capacity we can fast-track a Dedicated quote.
- Acceptance criteria (for moving to paid): 
  - Gate A: malformed-schema rate < 2% on the edge-case corpus
  - Gate B: per-field exactness >= 95% for required fields (invoice_number, total, tax, vendor_id)
  - Gate C: average median latency <= 350ms for single-call path

Operational next steps:
- We’ll produce a canary rollout plan after the baseline run: 1% traffic -> 10% -> 50% -> 100% with rollback thresholds tied to malformed rate and error spike.
- Please share procurement contact and whether Redwoods' standard MSA requires any special SSO/KMS notes.

Elena — great, thanks for the confirm. A few quick replies: 

1) Business-level validation: we’ll reject at runtime only for structural/schema failures. For arithmetic/business checks we’ll surface a "business_validation_fail" and include both modeled value and the corrected suggestion (when available) so you can decide programmatic acceptance.

2) Dedupe token: use header X-Client-Token. If you supply it Redwood will perform request dedupe (at-most-once) for TTL=48h. We also return request_id in the function response so you can reconcile.

3) Prompt tuning: Monica is right — explicit system instruction + few-shot pairs yield the best gains. We’ll iterate on 2–3 prompt templates during the trial and include those results in the baseline report.

Confirming the meeting: Wed, 24 May 2028 10:00am PT — I’ve sent a calendar hold. We’ll kick off the baseline job on Monday as soon as you upload both the sample_100_invoices.zip and the edge_cases set.
